1.1: God, who spoke to our ancestors in different ways and at different times through the prophets,
1.2: Has now spoken to us through His Son, the One He appointed to inherit everything, through whom He also made the universe.
1.3: The Son is the brightness of God's glory and the exact image of God's being, and He's holding everything together by the power of His word. After He purified our sins, He sat down at the right hand of God's majesty on high.
1.4: He became way better than the angels, 'cause He inherited a name that's more excellent than theirs.
1.5: Which of the angels did God ever say, "You are My Son, today I've begotten You"? And again, "I will be to Him a Father, And He shall be to Me a Son"?
1.6: And when He brings the firstborn into the world, He says, "Let all the angels of God worship Him."
1.7: And of the angels, He says, "He makes His angels spirits and His servants a flame of fire."
1.8: But to the Son, He says, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; The scepter of righteousness is the scepter of Your kingdom.
1.9: You loved righteousness and hated wickedness; So God, Your God, anointed You With the oil of joy more than Your companions."
1.10: And, "You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth, And the heavens are the work of Your hands.
1.11: They will pass away, but You stay the same; And they will all wear out like old clothes;
1.12: Like a cloak, You'll fold them up, And they'll be changed. But You are the same, And Your years will never end."
1.13: But to which of the angels did God ever say, "Sit at My right hand, Until I make Your enemies Your footstool"?
1.14: Aren't they all just ministering spirits, sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?

2.1: So, we gotta pay close attention to everything we've heard, don't let it slip away from us.
2.2: If the message given through angels was solid, and every mistake and disobedience got what it deserved,
2.3: How we gonna escape if we neglect this great salvation, which first came from Jesus, and was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,
2.4: With God showing up with signs, wonders, miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, doing what He wills?
2.5: He ain't put the world to come under the control of angels,
2.6: But someone testified somewhere, saying: "What is man that You think about him, Or the son of man that You care for him?
2.7: You made him a little lower than the angels, You crowned him with glory and honor, And put him in charge of everything You made.
2.8: You put all things under his feet." But now, we don't see everything under his feet yet, but we do see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels,
2.9: For the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor, so He could taste death for everyone, by God's grace.
2.10: It was only right for the One who made everything and through whom everything exists, to bring many sons to glory by perfecting their Captain (Jesus) through suffering.
2.11: Both Jesus, who sanctifies, and those who are being sanctified, are one family, which is why He ain't ashamed to call us His brothers and sisters,
2.12: Saying: "I'll declare Your name to My family; I'll sing Your praises among them."
2.13: And again, "I'll put My trust in Him." And again: "Here I am, and the children God gave Me."
2.14: Since the children share in flesh and blood, He also shared in the same stuff, so that through death, He could destroy the one who had power over death—the devil,
2.15: And free those who've been living in fear of death, in bondage their whole lives.
2.16: He didn't come to help angels, but He came to help Abraham's descendants.
2.17: So, He had to be like His brothers and sisters in every way, so He could be a merciful and faithful High Priest, making atonement for the sins of the people.
2.18: And since He suffered and was tempted, He knows how to help those who are tempted.

3.1: So, holy brothers and sisters, you who are partakers in this heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of our faith,
3.2: Who was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just like Moses was faithful in God's house.
3.3: But Jesus, the One we're talking about, has more glory than Moses, because the One who built the house has more honor than the house itself.
3.4: Every house is built by someone, but God built everything.
3.5: Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant, giving us a testimony of what was to come,
3.6: But Christ is over His own house as a Son, and we are that house, if we hold on tight to our confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm till the end.
3.7: So, just like the Holy Spirit says: "Today, if you hear His voice,
3.8: Don't harden your hearts like your people did in the rebellion, In the day they were tested in the wilderness,
3.9: Where your ancestors tested Me, tried Me, And saw all the things I did for forty years.
3.10: So I was mad at that generation, And said, 'They always go astray in their hearts, And they don't know My ways.'
3.11: So I swore in My anger, 'They ain't gonna enter My rest.'"
3.12: Watch out, fam, don't let any of you have an evil heart of unbelief, turning away from the living God.
3.13: But keep encouraging each other daily while it's still "today," so none of you get hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
3.14: We've become partakers of Christ if we hold onto our confidence all the way to the end.
3.15: Just like it says: "Today, if you hear His voice, Don't harden your hearts like they did in the rebellion."
3.16: Who heard and rebelled? Wasn't it everyone who came out of Egypt, led by Moses?
3.17: And who was God mad at for forty years? Wasn't it those who sinned, whose bodies dropped dead in the wilderness?
3.18: And to whom did He swear they wouldn't enter His rest? Only the ones who didn't obey.
3.19: So we see that they couldn't get in because of unbelief.

4.1: Since there's still a promise for us to enter God's rest, we need to be careful and make sure none of us miss out.
4.2: The gospel was preached to us just like it was to them, but the word they heard didn't do them any good 'cause they didn't mix it with faith.
4.3: But we who believe enter that rest, just like He said: "I swore in My anger, 'They ain't gon' enter My rest,'" Even though the works were finished since the world began.
4.4: God said this on the seventh day: "God rested on the seventh day from all His works."
4.5: And again He said: "They ain't gon' enter My rest."
4.6: Since some gotta enter it, and the people who first heard the gospel didn't enter 'cause of their disobedience,
4.7: God set aside a new day, calling it "Today," through David, after a long time: "Today, if you hear His voice, Don't harden your hearts."
4.8: If Joshua had given them rest, God wouldn't be talking about another day.
4.9: So, there's still a rest for the people of God.
4.10: Those who enter God's rest stop doing their works, just like God stopped His.
4.11: So, let's make sure we're diligent to enter that rest, so we don't fall into the same disobedience as those before us.
4.12: The Word of God is alive and powerful, sharper than any two-edged sword. It cuts deep—dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It discerning your thoughts and what's in your heart.
4.13: There's nothing hidden from His sight—everything is open to Him, and we gotta give an account to Him for everything.
4.14: Since we got a great High Priest, who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let's hold on to our confession.
4.15: We don't have a High Priest who doesn't understand our struggles. He's been through the same temptations we face, but He didn't sin.
4.16: So let's come boldly to the throne of grace, so we can get mercy and find grace to help us when we need it.

5.1: Every high priest, chosen from among men, is put in charge to handle stuff that concerns God, so he can offer gifts and sacrifices for sin.
5.2: He's supposed to have compassion on those who don't know better and are wandering, 'cause he himself gets caught up in weakness too.
5.3: That's why he has to offer sacrifices for his own sins, and for the people's too.
5.4: No one just takes this honor for themselves. Only the ones God calls to it, just like He did for Aaron.
5.5: Christ didn't try to glorify Himself to be High Priest. Nah, it was God who said to Him: "You are My Son, Today I have begotten You."
5.6: He also says in another part: "You are a priest forever According to the order of Melchizedek."
5.7: In His human form, Jesus cried out vehemently, praying and pleading with God, the One who could save Him from death, and God heard Him because He was truly God-fearing.
5.8: Even though He was the Son of God, He still had to learn obedience through everything He suffered.
5.9: And after going through all of that, He was perfected, becoming the author of eternal salvation for everyone who obeys Him,
5.10: And He was called by God as High Priest in the order of Melchizedek.
5.11: We got a lot to say about Melchizedek, but it's hard to explain 'cause y'all aren't really hearing right now.
5.12: By now, y'all should be teaching others, but you still need someone to teach you the basics of God's Word. You're still on that milk, not ready for solid food.
5.13: Anyone who only drinks milk ain't skilled in the word of righteousness—they're just a baby in the faith.
5.14: But if you're grown in the faith, you're eating solid food, meaning you've been through some things and learned how to discern between good and evil. You're not out here getting caught up in every little thing anymore.

6.1: So, let's move beyond the basics of Christ and go on to maturity. We ain't gon' keep going over the same things like repentance from dead works and having faith in God,
6.2: Or talkin' about baptisms, laying on of hands, resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
6.3: We'll do all this if God permits.
6.4: But here's the deal: If someone has been enlightened, tasted the heavenly gift, been filled with the Holy Spirit,
6.5: And has tasted the goodness of God's word and experienced the powers of the world to come,
6.6: But they fall away, it's impossible to bring them back to repentance, because they're crucifying Christ again and putting Him to open shame.
6.7: The earth gets rain, and when it drinks it up, it brings forth good things for those who work it, so it's blessed by God.
6.8: But if it brings thorns and thistles, it gets rejected and is almost cursed—its end is to be burned.
6.9: But we believe in better things for you, things that go with salvation, even though we're saying all this.
6.10: God ain't gon' forget the work you've put in and the love you've shown for His name. You've served the saints, and you're still out here serving.
6.11: We want each one of you to stay diligent and keep your hope strong until the end,
6.12: So you don't get lazy, but follow the examples of those who, through faith and patience, inherit the promises.
6.13: When God made a promise to Abraham, He couldn't swear by anyone greater, so He swore by Himself,
6.14: Saying, "For sure, I will bless you, and I will multiply you."
6.15: After waiting patiently, Abraham received what was promised.
6.16: People swear by something greater than themselves, and when they make an oath, it settles things.
6.17: God wanted to show the heirs of promise just how unchangeable His plans are, so He confirmed His promise with an oath.
6.18: God can't lie, and because of that, we can find strong comfort in His promise, especially those of us who've fled to Him for refuge, holding on to the hope that's in front of us.
6.19: This hope is like an anchor for our souls—steady and secure, and it reaches all the way into God's presence behind the veil.
6.20: Jesus is the forerunner, and He's entered for us, becoming our High Priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.

7.1: Now, Melchizedek, the king of Salem and the priest of the Most High God, met Abraham when he was coming back from defeating the kings and blessed him.
7.2: Abraham gave him a tenth of everything, and Melchizedek's name means "king of righteousness," and he's also called the king of peace.
7.3: He didn't have a father or mother, no genealogy, no beginning or end to his life—he was like the Son of God, a priest forever.
7.4: Consider how great this man was, even Abraham, the patriarch, gave him a tenth of the spoils.
7.5: Now, the sons of Levi, who receive the priesthood, are commanded to collect tithes from their people, but Melchizedek, who ain't from their family line, received tithes from Abraham and blessed him, the one who had the promises.
7.6: So, the lesser (Abraham) was blessed by the greater (Melchizedek).
7.7: No debate—the lesser is always blessed by the greater.
7.8: Here, regular men receive tithes, but over there, Melchizedek gets them, and it's testified that he's still alive.
7.9: Even Levi, who's supposed to receive the tithes, paid tithes through Abraham, in a way.
7.10: He was still in Abraham's loins when Melchizedek met him.
7.11: So, if the Levitical priesthood could bring perfection (and under it, the law was given), why would we need another priest like Melchizedek to rise up? Why not just stick to the Aaronic line?
7.12: If the priesthood changes, the law has to change too.
7.13: For the priest we're talking about is from another tribe, the tribe of Judah, and Moses didn't speak about priesthood coming from there.
7.14: It's clear that our Lord came from Judah, and that tribe wasn't ever about priesthood.
7.15: But it's even more clear that, just like Melchizedek, another priest who looks like him has come,
7.16: And He ain't come based on fleshly rules but by the power of an endless life.
7.17: God said to Him: "You are a priest forever, According to the order of Melchizedek."
7.18: The old commandment was canceled 'cause it wasn't doing the job—it was weak and didn't bring perfection.
7.19: But now we got a better hope because of the new priesthood, and it's that hope that brings us closer to God.
7.20: And since Jesus wasn't made a priest just like the others, but He was made a priest with an oath from God Himself,
7.21: He became a surety of a better covenant.
7.22: The old priests had to die off, but Jesus? He lives forever, and His priesthood is unchangeable.
7.23: The old priests couldn't keep going because of death,
7.24: But Jesus, because He lives forever, has a priesthood that doesn't change.
7.25: And because of that, He's able to save to the uttermost everyone who comes to God through Him—He's always interceding for us.
7.26: He's the perfect High Priest for us—holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and greater than the heavens.
7.27: Unlike the old high priests, He didn't need to offer sacrifices every day—first for His own sins, then for the people's. He did it once, and He offered up Himself.
7.28: The law appointed men who have weaknesses as high priests, but God's oath appoints the Son, who has been perfected forever.

8.1: Now here's the main thing I'm tryna say: We got us a High Priest who's sitting at the right hand of God's throne in heaven,
8.2: He's the Minister of the true sanctuary, the real tabernacle that God built, not man.
8.3: Every high priest is called to offer gifts and sacrifices. So, this One—Jesus—had to have something to offer too.
8.4: If He was on earth, He wouldn't be a priest, 'cause there are already priests doing the work of offering gifts according to the law,
8.5: They're serving a copy and shadow of what's in heaven—just like Moses was told by God to make the tabernacle according to the pattern He showed him on the mountain.
8.6: But now Jesus has a better ministry. He's the Mediator of a better covenant, built on better promises.
8.7: If the first covenant was perfect, we wouldn't need a new one.
8.8: But God found something wrong with it, so He said: "The days are coming," says the Lord, "When I'm gonna make a new covenant with Israel and Judah,
8.9: Not like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I led them outta Egypt. They didn't keep it, and I disregarded them," says the Lord.
8.10: "This is the covenant I'm gonna make with Israel after those days," says the Lord: "I'm gon' put My laws in their minds, And write them on their hearts. I'll be their God, and they'll be My people.
8.11: Nobody's gon' have to teach their neighbor or tell their brother, 'Know the Lord,' 'Cause everyone's gon' know Me, from the least to the greatest.
8.12: I'm gon' be merciful to their wickedness, And their sins and evil deeds, I ain't gon' remember them no more."
8.13: Since God said, "A new covenant," that means the first one's done. Now what's getting old and outdated is ready to disappear.

9.1: Now, the first covenant had rules for worship and the earthly sanctuary.
9.2: A tabernacle was set up: the first part had the lampstand, the table, and the showbread—that part's called the sanctuary,
9.3: And behind the second veil, there was the Holiest of All—
9.4: This had the golden censer and the ark of the covenant covered in gold, with stuff like the golden pot of manna, Aaron's rod, and the tablets of the covenant.
9.5: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. But yo, we ain't got time to go into all these details right now.
9.6: When all this was set up, the priests always went into the first part of the tabernacle, doing the services,
9.7: But only the high priest went into the second part, and that was only once a year, and not without blood, which he offered for himself and the people's sins done in ignorance.
9.8: The Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Holiest of All wasn't open as long as the first tabernacle was standing.
9.9: This was a symbol for the present time, where both gifts and sacrifices were offered, but they couldn't really make the person performing the service perfect in their conscience—
9.10: It was all about food, drink, washings, and fleshly rules, until the time when everything would change.
9.11: But Christ came as the High Priest of the better things to come, with a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with human hands, that is, not of this creation.
9.12: He didn't come with the blood of goats and calves, but with His own blood, He entered the Most Holy Place once for all, and secured eternal redemption.
9.13: If the blood of bulls, goats, and the ashes of a heifer could sanctify people for the purifying of their flesh,
9.14: How much more will Christ's blood, who through the eternal Spirit, offered Himself without blemish to God, cleanse our consciences from dead works so we can serve the living God?
9.15: And for this reason, He is the Mediator of the new covenant, by means of His death, for the redemption of the sins under the first covenant. Now those who are called can receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
9.16: For where there's a will, there must also be a death of the one who made the will.
9.17: A will is only in effect once the person is dead, because it doesn't have any power while the testator is still alive.
9.18: That's why even the first covenant wasn't set up without blood.
9.19: When Moses spoke the law to the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, mixed with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book and all the people,
9.20: Saying, "This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you."
9.21: Then he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the ministry vessels with the blood.
9.22: According to the law, almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood, there's no forgiveness.
9.23: It was necessary for the earthly copies of heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves need better sacrifices.
9.24: Christ didn't go into the man-made holy places, which are just copies of the real thing. He went into heaven itself to appear in God's presence for us.
9.25: He didn't have to offer Himself over and over, like the high priest does every year with someone else's blood—
9.26: If He did, He would've had to suffer from the beginning of time. But now, at the end of the ages, He came to put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself.
9.27: And just as it's appointed for men to die once, and after that the judgment,
9.28: Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many. And those who are waiting for Him, He will appear a second time, but this time, it won't be about dealing with sin, but for salvation.

10.1: So look, the law was just a shadow of the good stuff to come, not the real deal. These sacrifices they offer every year can't make anyone perfect.
10.2: If they could, they would've stopped offering them, because once people were purified, they wouldn't even be thinking about their sins anymore.
10.3: But every year, these sacrifices just remind them of their sins.
10.4: It's impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
10.5: So when Christ came into the world, He said: "Sacrifice and offering You didn't want, But You prepared a body for Me.
10.6: You didn't take pleasure in burnt offerings or sin offerings,
10.7: Then I said, 'Here I am, I've come— To do Your will, O God.'"
10.8: Before He said this, He said, "Sacrifice and offering, burnt offerings, and sin offerings, You didn't want or take pleasure in," (which are all the stuff according to the law),
10.9: Then He said, "Here I am to do Your will, O God." So, He takes away the old system to set up the new one.
10.10: By this will we are sanctified through the offering of Jesus Christ's body, once and for all.
10.11: Every priest stands and offers the same sacrifices over and over, but none of them can take away sins.
10.12: But Jesus, after offering Himself as the one sacrifice for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,
10.13: From then on, waiting for His enemies to become His footstool.
10.14: By that one offering, He perfected forever those who are being sanctified.
10.15: And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after He said:
10.16: "This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put My laws in their hearts, and write them on their minds."
10.17: Then He added, "Their sins and lawless deeds, I won't remember anymore."
10.18: And where there's forgiveness of these, there's no more sacrifice for sin.
10.19: So, brothers and sisters, since we have boldness to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus,
10.20: By the new and living way He opened for us through the veil, that is, His flesh,
10.21: And since we have a High Priest over the house of God,
10.22: Let's draw near with a true heart and full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
10.23: Let's hold on tight to the confession of our hope without wavering, 'cause He who promised is faithful.
10.24: And let's think about each other, to stir up love and good works,
10.25: Not skipping out on meeting together, like some do, but encouraging each other—and even more as you see the Day getting closer.
10.26: If we sin willfully after we've received the truth, there's no longer any sacrifice for sins left,
10.27: But a fearful expectation of judgment and fiery anger that will devour those who oppose God.
10.28: Anyone who rejected Moses' law had to die without mercy by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
10.29: How much worse do you think it'll be for someone who has trampled on the Son of God, treated the blood of the covenant like it's nothing, and disrespected the Spirit of grace?
10.30: We know God said, "Vengeance is Mine, I will repay," and He will judge His people.
10.31: It's a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
10.32: But remember the past, when you first heard the truth, and endured through a hard struggle with sufferings,
10.33: Partly when people made a spectacle of you, with insults and trials,
10.34: And partly when you stood with those who were treated the same way. You had compassion on me in my chains and joyfully accepted the plundering of your stuff, knowing you got a better and lasting possession in heaven.
10.35: So don't throw away your confidence—it has a great reward.
10.36: You need to endure, so that after you've done what God called you to do, you can receive the promise:
10.37: "A little while longer, And He who is coming will come and won't delay.
10.38: But the just shall live by faith; If anyone turns back, My soul has no pleasure in them."
10.39: But we aren't the ones who turn back to destruction; we're the ones who believe to the saving of the soul.

11.1: So, faith is the substance of things we hope for, the evidence of things we ain't seen yet.
11.2: By it, the elders got a good testimony.
11.3: By faith, we understand that God framed the worlds with His word, so the stuff we see wasn't made from what we can see.
11.4: By faith, Abel offered a better sacrifice to God than Cain, and through it, he got recognized as righteous. God testified about his gifts, and even though he's dead, his faith still speaks.
11.5: By faith, Enoch was taken up and didn't see death—he was just gone, 'cause God took him. He had this testimony that he pleased God.
11.6: Without faith, it's impossible to please God. You gotta believe that He is, and that He rewards those who seek Him.
11.7: By faith, Noah, being warned about things that hadn't been seen, built the ark to save his family. By his faith, he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes from faith.
11.8: By faith, Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he didn't know, but he knew it would be his inheritance.
11.9: By faith, he lived in the promised land like a foreigner, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise.
11.10: He was waiting for the city with foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
11.11: By faith, Sarah received strength to conceive a child when she was past the age, 'cause she judged God faithful who made the promise.
11.12: So from one man, and he was basically dead, came descendants as many as the stars and the sand by the seashore—too many to count.
11.13: All these people died in faith, without receiving the promises, but they saw them from far off, were assured of them, embraced them, and confessed that they were just strangers and travelers on this earth.
11.14: They said they were looking for a homeland.
11.15: If they were thinking about the country they left, they could've gone back, but they were after something better, a heavenly country.
11.16: That's why God ain't ashamed to be called their God, 'cause He's got a city prepared for them.
11.17: By faith, Abraham, when tested, offered up Isaac, and he who had received the promises was about to sacrifice his only son,
11.18: Even though God said, "In Isaac your descendants will be called."
11.19: Abraham believed that God could even raise Isaac from the dead, and figuratively, he received him back from the dead.
11.20: By faith, Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the things to come.
11.21: By faith, Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons, and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
11.22: By faith, Joseph, when he was dying, spoke about the departure of the Israelites, and gave instructions about his bones.
11.23: By faith, Moses was hidden for three months by his parents 'cause they saw he was beautiful and weren't afraid of the king's orders.
11.24: By faith, when Moses grew up, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
11.25: Choosing rather to suffer with the people of God than to enjoy the temporary pleasures of sin.
11.26: He thought the reproach of Christ was more valuable than all the treasures in Egypt, because he was looking forward to the reward.
11.27: By faith, he left Egypt, not afraid of the king's anger, and endured as though he was seeing the Invisible One.
11.28: By faith, he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so the one who destroyed the firstborn wouldn't touch them.
11.29: By faith, they walked through the Red Sea like it was dry land, while the Egyptians drowned when they tried to do the same.
11.30: By faith, the walls of Jericho fell down after the Israelites marched around them for seven days.
11.31: By faith, Rahab, the prostitute, didn't perish with those who didn't believe when she hid the spies and made peace with them.
11.32: What more can I say? I don't have enough time to talk about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and all the prophets—
11.33: Who through faith conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness, received promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
11.34: Quenched fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong from weakness, became brave in battle, and made their enemies run.
11.35: Women received their dead back to life. Others were tortured, not accepting deliverance, so they could have a better resurrection.
11.36: Some faced mockings, scourgings, and even chains and imprisonment.
11.37: They were stoned, sawed in half, tempted, killed by the sword. They wandered in sheepskins and goatskins, poor and afflicted.
11.38: The world wasn't worthy of them. They lived in deserts, mountains, and caves—these were the faithful.
11.39: All these people, even though they had faith and got a good testimony, didn't receive the promises.
11.40: God had something better for us, so they couldn't be perfected without us.

12.1: So since we got this big ol' crowd of witnesses all around us, let's throw off anything weighin' us down and that sin that keep trippin' us up, and let's keep runnin' this race God set for us,
12.2: keepin' our eyes locked on Jesus, the one who started our faith and the one who gonna finish it. For the joy ahead of him, he went through the cross, brushed off the shame, and now he sittin' at the right hand of God's throne.
12.3: Think about him who took all that pushback from sinners, so you don't get tired and give up.
12.4: In your fight against sin, you ain't resisted to the point of sheddin' blood.
12.5: And you done forgot the word that encourage you like a father talkin' to his child? It say,
12.6: "My child, don't shrug off the Lord's discipline, and don't lose heart when he correct you,
12.7: 'cause the Lord disciplines who he love, and he correct everybody he accept as his child."
12.8: Take hardship as discipline; God treatin' you like his children. What child don't get disciplined by they father?
12.9: If you ain't gettin' disciplined--and everybody get discipline--then you ain't really his, you not true sons and daughters.
12.10: We all had human fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them for it. How much more should we submit to the Father of spirits and live!
12.11: They disciplined us for a little while how they thought was best; but God disciplines us for our good, so we can share in his holiness.
12.12: Discipline don't feel good at the time--it's painful. But later, it bring a harvest of right-livin' and peace to the ones trained by it.
12.13: So strengthen your weak arms and shaky knees.
12.14: "Make straight paths for your feet," so the lame won't get worse, but instead get healed.
12.15: Make every effort to live in peace with everybody and to be holy; without holiness nobody gon' see the Lord.
12.16: Watch out so nobody fall short of God's grace and no bitter root grow up to cause trouble and mess up a bunch of people.
12.17: Make sure nobody livin' sexually immoral, or godless like Esau, who traded away his birthright for one meal.
12.18: After that, you know, when he wanted the blessing, he got turned down. Even though he cried for it, he couldn't undo what he already did.
12.19: You ain't come to a mountain you can touch, burnin' with fire, with darkness, gloom, and storm,
12.20: to a trumpet blast or a voice so strong folks begged not to hear another word,
12.21: 'cause they couldn't handle what was commanded: "If even an animal touch the mountain, it must be stoned to death."
12.22: It was so scary Moses said, "I'm tremblin' with fear."
12.23: But you done come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You done come to thousands and thousands of angels in joyful assembly,
12.24: to the church of the firstborn whose names written in heaven. You done come to God, the Judge of all, to the spirits of righteous folks made perfect,
12.25: to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speak a better word than the blood of Abel.
12.26: Make sure you don't refuse the one who speak. If they ain't escape when they refused the one warnin' them on earth, how much less we gon' escape if we turn away from the one warnin' us from heaven?
12.27: Back then his voice shook the earth, but now he promised, "One more time I'll shake not just the earth but the heavens too."
12.28: That "one more time" mean what can be shaken--the created stuff--gonna be removed, so what can't be shaken will stay.
12.29: So since we gettin' a kingdom that can't be shaken, let's be grateful and worship God in a way he accept, with reverence and awe, 'cause our God is a consumin' fire.

13.1: Let that brotherly love keep going strong.
13.2: Don't forget to be kind to strangers, 'cause some people have entertained angels without even knowing it.
13.3: Remember those who are in prison, like you're right there with them. And those who are mistreated, 'cause you're also in this body.
13.4: Marriage is honorable for all, and the marriage bed is undefiled—but God will judge fornicators and adulterers.
13.5: Don't be out here chasing after stuff you don't have—be content with what you got. Remember, God said, "I will never leave you or forsake you."
13.6: So we can boldly say, "The Lord is my helper; I won't be afraid. What can man do to me?"
13.7: Remember those who lead you, who taught you the word of God, and follow their faith, considering how their lives ended.
13.8: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
13.9: Don't be caught up in all these weird doctrines. It's good for your heart to be strengthened by grace, not by food laws that ain't helped anyone.
13.10: We got an altar where those who serve the tabernacle ain't allowed to eat.
13.11: The bodies of those animals, whose blood the high priest took into the holy place for sin, are burned outside the camp.
13.12: And just like that, Jesus, to sanctify the people with His own blood, suffered outside the gate.
13.13: So, let's go to Him, outside the camp, and be willing to bear His reproach.
13.14: We don't have a permanent city here, but we're looking for the one to come.
13.15: So, through Jesus, let's keep offering the sacrifice of praise to God—the fruit of our lips, thanking His name.
13.16: But don't forget to do good and share—God is pleased with these sacrifices.
13.17: Obey those who lead you, and be submissive to them, 'cause they're watching out for your souls, and they gotta give an account. Let them do it with joy, not with grief, 'cause that's unprofitable for you.
13.18: Pray for us, 'cause we're sure that we have a good conscience and want to live honorably in everything.
13.19: I'm asking especially that you pray so I can be restored to you quicker.
13.20: Now, may the God of peace, who brought up our Lord Jesus from the dead, that great Shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,
13.21: Make you complete in every good work to do His will, working in you what's pleasing in His sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
13.22: I'm asking you, brothers and sisters, to bear with this word of encouragement, 'cause I've written to you in a few words.
13.23: Know that Timothy has been set free, and I'll see you soon if he comes.
13.24: Greet those who lead you, and all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.
13.25: Grace be with you all. Amen.
